title: Returning to the breath
summary: A gentle walk through presence, small rituals, and the quiet that was never gone — written in the same spirit as the Stillwater journal.

blocks.text: Nothing about this practice asks you to become someone new. The journal is only a frame: a little structure so your own words can land without having to be perfect.
Below, each part of this entry scrolls in order — one gentle section after another.
The mind loves a problem to solve. Sometimes the kindest thing is not to solve — only to notice.
The quieter you become, the more you are able to hear.

pairs.hidden: Not fixing your life in one breath — simply choosing the next kind, honest moment.

pairs.prompt: What is the risk of waiting for calm first?
pairs.hidden: Calm often arrives after we stop demanding it as a precondition.

blocks.text: Keep them small. Small is how they survive busy days.

sections.title: Arrive
sections.body: Feel feet on the floor, or hands on the page. One sentence about what is true right now.

sections.title: Listen
sections.body: Name one sound or sensation without judging it. Let it pass.

sections.title: Release
sections.body: Exhale a little longer than the inhale. Once is enough to count.

blocks.text: When you are tender, you might need warmth. When you are scattered, you might need clarity. Both can be true.

tabs.label: Heart
tabs.content: You are not behind. You are in motion — even rest is motion when chosen with care.

tabs.label: Mind
tabs.content: Name one variable you control today: a single breath, a single line of writing, one boundary kept kindly.

tabs.label: Body
tabs.content: Drop your shoulders. Unclench the jaw. The body often believes the story first.

blocks.text: Put these in an order that feels honest for a heavy day — then tap Check.

interaction.prompt: Arrange from what you’d do first to last:
items: Ask for one small help or pause
correctOrder: Ask for one small help or pause

blocks.text: Endings can be soft. Swipe through a few — one may be enough for today.

slides.title: A line to keep
slides.body: I do not have to earn rest. I can choose a gentler next minute.

slides.title: A question
slides.body: What would I say to a friend who felt exactly like this?

slides.title: A promise
slides.body: I will return to the page without needing to fix everything first.
